title: SETU — Hyderabad Monsoon Flood & Japanese Intervention Planner
resolution: 145 GHMC wards (open data; the city's 16 stormwater zones are not public)
limitations: Modelled at ward resolution, not street level — needs GHMC's private drain network for finer.

Which wards flood first is LEARNED from terrain & drainage features using flooded localities from 8 real floods (2016-09, 2020-10-13, 2021-07-14, 2023-07-27, 2025-06-12, 2025-07-18, 2025-09-18, 2026-06-09).

Tested on floods it never saw (leave-one-event-out): AUC 0.674 (0.5 = coin flip), and 0.659 when comparing wards of similar size, so it is not just 'big wards get named more'. One event (Jun-2026 junction waterlogging in central wards) scored near chance. Useful for ranking, not exact prediction.
Independent check against GHMC's own published chronic-waterlogging lists (never used in training): AUC 0.744.

Independent check against GHMC's official list of 248 flood-vulnerable localities: only weak-to-moderate agreement (AUC 0.577 for the densest quarter of wards) — that list reflects who lives near water, not only where water rose.
The 2020 validation map is NOT independent — 2020 is one of the events the model learned from.
The rainfall scale is anchored to documented extents (~3% of wards at 50 mm, ~20% at 192 mm, ~55% at 300 mm) — an assumption, not learned.
Rain is assumed equal over all wards ('what if X mm fell everywhere'); real storms are uneven (Oct 2020: ~197 mm Begumpet vs ~320 mm Ghatkesar).
Flood records are news-reported place names (presence-only, ~60 ward mentions); unnamed wards are unknown, not dry.
Flood depths are shallow ward-averages; severity is relative to the city distribution.
Intervention 'after' effect is a modelled estimate, not a hydraulic re-simulation.
Water bodies, nalas & roads from OpenStreetMap — some may be unmapped.
